prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
SNP Manifesto 2015 – “Stronger for Scotland” (summary)

Core goals
- Amplify Scotland’s voice at Westminster; pursue progressive alternatives to austerity.
- SNP will not put the Conservatives into power; will work with others to keep them out.
- Independence is not the focus of this election; seek stronger devolution/Home Rule.

Economy and public finances
- End austerity with modest, responsible increases in public spending each year while reducing deficit/debt as a share of income.
- Major investment in infrastructure, housing (UK target 100,000 affordable homes/yr), broadband/4G, and high‑speed rail linking Scotland and the north of England.
- Fairer taxation: restore 50p top rate; bankers’ bonus tax; higher bank levy; mansion tax; end non‑dom status; clamp down on avoidance; review pension tax relief; consider reversing married couples’ allowance.
- Create sovereign wealth/energy fund; expand Green Investment Bank; seed‑fund a Scottish Business Development Bank; maintain/expand Annual Investment Allowance; raise Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019‑20.
- Support SMEs with prompt‑payment protections and better access to export finance; cut/abolish Air Passenger Duty; consider VAT cut for hospitality.
- City Deals for all Scottish cities; rural support including a fair share of CAP convergence funds.

Jobs, pay and welfare
- Raise minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the Living Wage; curb exploitative zero‑hours contracts.
- Increase Universal Credit work allowance; scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt rollout of Universal Credit and PIP; reverse DLA–PIP switch; reform sanctions and disability assessments.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level; uprate benefits with cost of living; oppose restricting Housing Benefit for 18–21s.
- Pensions: maintain triple lock; set single‑tier at £160/week; protect Savings Credit; review state pension age rise; protect winter fuel allowance (incl. off‑grid early payment).

Public services and bills
- Increase NHS funding across the UK (worth £2bn more for Scotland by 2020‑21); oppose privatisation; integrate health and social care; expand mental health funding; more specialist nursing; retain free prescriptions and personal care.
- Cut energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation and enforcing pass‑through of wholesale price cuts.

Education and young people
- Expand free childcare to 30 hours/week for 3–4s and eligible 2s; keep university free.
- 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships annually; expand EMA; strengthen equal pay measures.

Energy, climate and environment
- Oppose Trident renewal and new nuclear; maintain fracking moratorium.
- Back offshore wind, hydro, CCS; reform transmission charging; deliver islands interconnector; expand community energy.
- Match Scotland’s carbon targets; establish a Climate Justice Fund; support global species protection.

Industry, regions and migration
- Support oil & gas jobs and supply chain; deploy Oil & Gas Authority in Aberdeen.
- Reintroduce post‑study work visa.
- Creative sector: fairer BBC Scotland share (+£100m); Creative Content Fund.

Democracy, rights and privacy
- Adopt STV for UK elections; abolish House of Lords; votes at 16; stronger MP recall.
- Protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; remove VAT on sanitary products.
- Advance equality: 50% women on public boards; equal pay audits; strengthen anti‑discrimination laws.
- Oppose blanket surveillance (“snoopers’ charter”); support targeted, overseen measures.

EU, foreign and defence
- Keep UK in the EU; “double‑majority” rule for any exit; protect public services in TTIP.
- Maintain 0.7% GNI aid; appoint LGBTI rights envoy; recognise Palestine; ensure lawful, Parliament‑approved military action.
- Strengthen conventional defence footprint in Scotland; procure Maritime Patrol Aircraft; ensure defence spending transparency.

Devolution
- Implement Smith Commission in full, then move to full fiscal responsibility.
- Prioritise devolution of employment policy (incl. minimum wage), welfare, taxation, National Insurance and equality; retain Barnett during transition.
